{"findings": [{"file": "src/ev/loop.zig", "line": 892, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "`Loop.add` still arms `.duration` timers from a stale `now`; only `setTimer` refreshes it", "body": "The fix refreshes the awake snapshot after a waiting backend poll, so the sleep no longer backdates a timer. It does not remove the defect at the site that owns it. `addInternal`'s `.timer` case calls `armTimer` directly (loop.zig:889-895), and `armTimer` computes a `.duration` deadline from `nowFor`, which returns the snapshot taken at the last `updateNow`. `setTimer` (loop.zig:634) calls `updateNow` first for exactly this reason; `add` does not. So the two arm paths compute deadlines against different clocks.

After the fix the residual staleness is the caller's run between two polls instead of the sleep, and that run is not small. The executor drains its whole ready batch between polls (runtime.zig:744-772). `tick_target_ns` is 100us, but the budget floor is 2 tasks and the clock checkpoint runs only every 127 quanta, so a task that does not yield holds the batch for as long as it runs.

Mechanism, concretely: two CPU-bound tasks run 50ms each after a poll returns; a third task then calls `timedWaitForIo(c, .fromMilliseconds(10))`, which arms the timeout with `group.add(&timer.c)` (src/common.zig:720) -> `Loop.add` -> `armTimer`. The deadline is `now_cached + 10ms`, and `now_cached` is 100ms old, so the deadline is already 90ms in the past. The next `checkTimers` fires it at once and `timedWaitForIo` returns `error.Timeout` before the I/O had any chance to run. The consequence is a spuriously expired I/O timeout under CPU load, the same user-visible symptom the commit fixes for the sleep case.

The fix that closes the class rather than one instance is to refresh in the arm path: call `self.state.updateNow()` in `addInternal`'s `.timer` case (or inside `armTimer` for the `.duration` arm), matching `setTimer`. That is safe for the same reason `setTimer`'s call is: both run on the owning thread, and advancing `tick` mid-scan only re-reads the boot/real caches."}, {"file": "src/ev/test/timer.zig", "line": 347, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "The regression test does not assert its own precondition, so it can pass vacuously", "body": "The test reproduces the bug only if the backend poll really slept across the writer thread's 1200ms delay. Nothing in the test checks that it did. The only assertions are on the timer's elapsed time, and those also hold when the read completes without any long poll.

Mechanism: if a later change makes the read completion arrive by some path that does not sleep in `backend.poll` (a thread-pool route because `pollable` is no longer honored, a wake that turns `backend_timeout` to `.zero`, a backend that returns early), the `while` loop at line 347 spins, `now` is never stale, the timer is armed correctly, and the test reports success. The output of a vacuous run is byte-identical to a real one, so the narrowing is silent and the test keeps guarding nothing.

Make the precondition observable: sample the monotonic clock before the `while` loop and assert that the read loop consumed at least ~1000ms, so a run in which the poll never slept fails instead of passing."}]}
